_provenance.notes: The Upper Cook Inlet (UCI) salmon fishery is Alaska's most politically charged allocation battleground. The Board of Fisheries meets triennially to adjust the Upper Cook Inlet Salmon Management Plan, balancing: (1) Commercial Drift Gillnetters, (2) Commercial East Side Setnetters (ESSN), (3) In-river Sport Anglers on the Kenai/Kasilof, and (4) Personal Use Dipnetters. The 2014 and 2020 Board of Fisheries decisions established strict paired restrictions linking ESSN commercial closures directly to Kenai River late-run Chinook escapement.

allocation_plan_milestones.event: First formal Upper Cook Inlet Management Plan adopted by BOF
allocation_plan_milestones.impact: Established priority for Kenai River sockeye escapement over commercial harvest targets.

allocation_plan_milestones.event: Personal Use Dipnet Fishery formalized as permanent allocation
allocation_plan_milestones.impact: Guaranteed 250k-500k sockeye allocation to Alaska residents at Kenai/Kasilof river mouths.

allocation_plan_milestones.event: Paired Restrictions Rule established for East Side Setnet (ESSN)
allocation_plan_milestones.impact: If Kenai late-run Chinook is projected below 15,000 large fish, ESSN commercial sockeye fishery is automatically restricted/closed.

allocation_plan_milestones.event: Optimal Escapement Goal (OEG) for Kenai late-run Chinook raised to 15,000-30,000
allocation_plan_milestones.impact: Resulted in extended commercial ESSN closures in 2021, 2022, and 2023.
